name: ser for who and what
instruction: Saying who somebody is, where they are from, or what they do.

name: estar for where
instruction: Saying where somebody or something is right now.

name: estar for how
instruction: How somebody feels or how something is at the moment.

name: hay against estar
instruction: Saying something exists somewhere, against locating a known thing.
examples: Hay una farmacia en la esquina
La farmacia está en la esquina

name: Noun gender
instruction: A noun taking an article or adjective, so the gender is visible.

name: Articles and adjectives agree
instruction: A plural or feminine noun with an article and an adjective.

name: Verb endings
instruction: A subject other than yo, where the ending changes.

name: Stem-changing verbs
instruction: A present-tense verb whose stem changes: querer, poder, pedir.

name: Dropping the subject pronoun
instruction: A subject already clear from the verb, with nothing contrasted.

name: no before the verb
instruction: A plain denial.

name: Question words first
instruction: A question with qué, dónde, cuándo or cómo, the subject after the verb.

name: ir a plus infinitive
instruction: A plan or something about to happen.

name: estar plus gerund
instruction: An action under way right now.

name: gustar
instruction: Liking something, where the thing liked is the subject.

name: Reflexive verbs
instruction: A daily routine, where English needs no pronoun.

name: States with tener
instruction: Being hungry, cold, afraid, right, or a certain age.

name: tener que
instruction: Something somebody has to do.

name: Weather with hacer
instruction: Talking about the weather.

name: tú against usted
instruction: Addressing a stranger, an older person, or a friend.

name: ustedes for all plural you
instruction: Addressing two or more people, friends included.

name: Fixed politeness
instruction: Asking a stranger for something in a shop or on the street.

name: me gustaría, quisiera
instruction: Ordering or requesting, in the fixed polite forms only.

name: ojalá
instruction: Hoping for something, as a fixed reply.

name: The imperative
instruction: Telling somebody to do something, tú or usted.

name: mi, tu, su, nuestro
instruction: Whose something is, the possessive agreeing with the thing owned.

name: The article on a generic noun
instruction: Liking or describing something in general, where English uses no article.

name: Adjective after the noun
instruction: A description whose adjective English puts in front.

name: al and del
instruction: Going to or coming from a place that takes el.

name: a against en
instruction: Going somewhere against being there.

name: muy against mucho
instruction: Intensifying an adjective, against a noun or a verb.

name: Tap r against trilled rr
instruction: A word with rr or initial r, next to one with a single r.

name: The preterite
instruction: A finished event at a stated time.

name: Irregular preterites
instruction: A finished event with ir, ser, tener, hacer, estar or poder.

name: The imperfect
instruction: How things used to be, or what was going on at the time.

name: The present perfect
instruction: Experience up to now, ever or never.

name: The simple future
instruction: A prediction or a promise further off than tonight.

name: acabar de
instruction: Something finished moments ago.

name: desde hace, hace … que
instruction: How long something has been going on and still is.
examples: Vivo aquí desde hace tres años
Hace una hora que te espero

name: ya, todavía, ya no
instruction: Something already done, not done yet, or no longer the case.

name: lo, la, los, las
instruction: Replacing a stated object — English speakers repeat the noun instead.

name: le, les
instruction: Giving, telling or showing something to somebody.

name: le with a named person
instruction: An indirect object named outright, which still takes le.
examples: Les mandé un mensaje a mis amigos

name: Pronouns with an infinitive or gerund
instruction: An object pronoun with ir a, querer or estar plus gerund.

name: Pronouns with the imperative
instruction: Telling somebody to do it, then telling them not to.

name: encantar, doler, importar
instruction: An ache, a pleasure or a concern, built like gustar.

name: se for each other
instruction: Two people doing something to one another.

name: que and donde
instruction: Joining two statements about the same person, thing or place.

name: mí, ti, conmigo, contigo
instruction: A pronoun after a preposition.

name: Personal a
instruction: A specific person as direct object.

name: por against para
instruction: A purpose or a recipient, against a cause or a route.

name: más, menos, tan … que
instruction: Setting two things side by side, or naming the best of a group.
examples: el mejor restaurante de la ciudad

name: saber against conocer
instruction: Knowing a fact or a skill against knowing a person or a place.

name: ir against venir
instruction: Moving toward the listener, where English says coming.

name: hay que
instruction: A general obligation with nobody in particular responsible.

name: The negative imperative
instruction: Telling somebody not to do something.

name: si with the present
instruction: A real condition and what will follow from it.

name: que te vaya bien
instruction: A goodbye or a good wish, in fixed form.

name: no … nada, nadie, nunca
instruction: Nothing, nobody or never after the verb, with no before it.

name: algún against ningún
instruction: Asking whether there is any, or saying there is none.

name: también against tampoco
instruction: Agreeing with a negative statement.

name: Gender against the ending
instruction: A noun whose gender its ending hides.

name: Preterite against imperfect
instruction: A narrative with both a background and an event.
examples: Estaba en la regadera cuando sonó el teléfono

name: The pluperfect
instruction: Something already over before another past event.
examples: Ya se había ido cuando llegué

name: The future for guessing
instruction: Guessing about the present.

name: llevar plus gerund
instruction: How long somebody has been doing something.

name: seguir, dejar de, volver a
instruction: Continuing, stopping or doing something again.

name: Subjunctive after wanting
instruction: Wanting, asking or hoping that somebody else does something.

name: Subjunctive after feeling
instruction: Being glad, sorry or afraid about what somebody else does.
examples: Me da gusto que estés bien

name: cuando about the future
instruction: Something to do once another future thing happens.

name: para que
instruction: Doing something so that somebody else can do something.
examples: Te lo digo para que sepas
Habla más fuerte para que te oigan

name: ojalá plus subjunctive
instruction: Hoping something happens.

name: es importante que
instruction: Judging what somebody else should do.

name: creo que against no creo que
instruction: Believing something, against doubting it.

name: The conditional to soften
instruction: A request or advice pitched short of an order.

name: si with the imperfect subjunctive
instruction: An unreal present condition and what would follow.
examples: Si yo fuera tú, no iría

name: Adjectives that change with ser and estar
instruction: An adjective whose meaning shifts between ser and estar.

name: ser for where an event is
instruction: Saying where a party, a meeting or a concert takes place.
examples: La fiesta es en casa de Ana

name: estar plus participle
instruction: The state something is left in.

name: se lo
instruction: Both objects as pronouns, one of them le.
examples: Se lo di a mi hermano

name: Impersonal se
instruction: What people in general do, with nobody named.

name: se me olvidó
instruction: An accident, told as something that happened to you.

name: lo que
instruction: The thing that, left unnamed.

name: por and para beyond the basics
instruction: A price, a duration, a deadline or an opinion.

name: Verbs with a fixed preposition
instruction: A verb whose preposition English does not have.

name: antes de, después de plus infinitive
instruction: One thing before or after another, the same person doing both.
examples: Antes de salir, cierra la puerta

name: que cannot be dropped
instruction: Reporting what somebody said or thinks, where English can leave out 'that'.

name: si and question words in reported questions
instruction: Reporting a question instead of asking it.

name: The infinitive as a noun
instruction: An activity as subject or object, where English uses -ing.

name: pero against sino
instruction: Correcting a negative statement.

name: porque, como, ya que
instruction: A reason the listener already knows, against one they do not.

name: ni … ni
instruction: Neither one thing nor the other.
examples: No tengo ni tiempo ni dinero

name: Diminutives
instruction: Softening a request or an offer in conversation.

name: Verbs that shift in the preterite
instruction: conocer, saber, querer or poder as an event rather than a state.

name: Reported speech in the past
instruction: Reporting what somebody said, from a past vantage point.

name: The future perfect
instruction: Something finished by a point still to come, or a guess about the past.

name: Passive with ser
instruction: A news report where the agent is secondary.

name: al plus infinitive
instruction: The moment one thing happens, triggering another.

name: Imperfect subjunctive after a past verb
instruction: Wanting or asking in the past that somebody else do something.

name: The present perfect subjunctive
instruction: Hoping, doubting or being glad about something already done.
examples: No creo que lo haya hecho

name: aunque with either mood
instruction: Conceding a known fact, against a possibility.

name: Subjunctive in a relative clause
instruction: Looking for something that may not exist.
examples: Busco a alguien que hable inglés

name: antes de que, sin que, hasta que
instruction: A conjunction leaving the second clause unrealised.

name: si with the pluperfect subjunctive
instruction: Regretting how something turned out.
examples: Si hubiera sabido, no habría venido
Si me hubieras avisado, te habría esperado

name: como si
instruction: Comparing with something untrue.
examples: Habla como si fuera el jefe
Me trata como si fuera un niño

name: tal vez against a lo mejor
instruction: Saying maybe, with tal vez or quizás taking the subjunctive and a lo mejor not.

name: siempre y cuando, con tal de que
instruction: A condition that must hold for something to go ahead.
examples: Voy, siempre y cuando me invites
Con tal de que llegues, no importa la hora

name: el que, la que after a preposition
instruction: A relative clause whose verb needs a preposition.
examples: la persona con la que hablé
la empresa en la que trabajo

name: lo and la for usted
instruction: A direct object meaning you, said to somebody addressed as usted.

name: Fronted object with a pronoun
instruction: Fronting the object to set the topic, which then needs lo or la.

name: lo cual, lo que for a whole clause
instruction: Commenting on everything just said.
examples: Llegó tarde, lo cual molestó a todos
No llamó, lo que me extrañó

name: se with a plural thing
instruction: Something done to plural things, with nobody named.

name: de que after a noun or adjective
instruction: A clause after a phrase that takes de.
examples: Me di cuenta de que era tarde

name: ponerse, volverse, hacerse
instruction: Somebody becoming something, temporarily or for good.

name: sin embargo, en cambio
instruction: Setting one fact against another inside an argument.
examples: Es caro; sin embargo, vale la pena
Él trabaja; ella, en cambio, estudia

name: entre más … más
instruction: The more one thing happens, the more another does.
examples: Entre más lo pienso, menos lo entiendo

name: hacer falta, valer la pena
instruction: Needing something, or judging whether it is worth it.

name: mandar a hacer
instruction: Having somebody else do something for you.
examples: Me corté el pelo en el centro

name: ándale, órale, pásale
instruction: Urging or welcoming somebody in casual Mexican speech.
examples: Córrele, que se va el camión

name: no es que
instruction: Rejecting a reason before giving the real one.
examples: No es que no quiera, es que no puedo

name: pase lo que pase
instruction: Whatever happens, nothing changes the outcome.
examples: Pase lo que pase, te apoyo
Sea como sea, hay que terminar

name: el hecho de que
instruction: A known fact as the subject of a judgement.
examples: El hecho de que no llame me preocupa

name: por mucho que, por más que
instruction: However much somebody tries, nothing changes.
examples: Por mucho que insistas, no voy
Por más que lo intento, no me sale

name: de plus infinitive as a condition
instruction: A condition compressed into an infinitive.
examples: De haberlo sabido, no habría venido
De seguir así, nos vamos a perder

name: The conditional for unverified claims
instruction: Reporting something the press has not confirmed.
examples: El sospechoso habría huido a Guatemala
El costo superaría los mil millones

name: ha de for probability
instruction: A confident guess, in Mexican speech.

name: acabar por, terminar plus gerund
instruction: How something ended up after resistance.

name: habiendo plus participle
instruction: A written clause saying what had already been done.
examples: Habiendo terminado el informe, se fue

name: cuyo
instruction: A written relative naming what belongs to somebody.
examples: una empresa cuyos dueños viven fuera

name: quien for whoever
instruction: Anyone at all who does something.

name: fue ahí donde, es él quien
instruction: Insisting it was this one and not another.
examples: Es él quien tiene que decidir

name: lo plus adjective plus que
instruction: Exclaiming how much of a quality something has.
examples: No sabes lo cansado que estoy

name: no obstante, asimismo, por ende
instruction: Turning or extending a written argument.

name: Nominalisation
instruction: A headline or a report where the action becomes a noun.
examples: La cancelación del vuelo fue confirmada

name: llevar a cabo, dar a conocer
instruction: A formal report where the verb carries little of the meaning.
examples: Se llevó a cabo una revisión
El gobierno dio a conocer las cifras

name: dizque
instruction: Reporting a claim you doubt, in casual Mexican speech.

name: The future subjunctive
instruction: Legal text or a fixed saying.
examples: Adonde fueres, haz lo que vieres

name: The -se imperfect subjunctive
instruction: Formal prose using the -se forms.
examples: Si tuviese más tiempo, lo haría

name: -ra as a pluperfect
instruction: Journalistic or literary prose looking back to an earlier past.
examples: el edificio que fuera su casa

name: Mixed conditionals
instruction: A past condition with a present result.
examples: Si hubiera estudiado, ahora sería médico
Si no fuera tan terco, ya lo habría arreglado

name: Verbs that switch meaning with mood
instruction: decir or sentir, reporting with the indicative and ordering or regretting with the subjunctive.
examples: Le dije que venía / Le dije que viniera
Siento que alguien me sigue / Siento que estés mal

name: ni que
instruction: Rejecting a claim as absurd.

name: con lo que
instruction: Complaining that something happened in spite of an obvious fact.
examples: Con lo que gana, y se queja
Con lo caro que está, ni lo compres

name: Fronting the predicate
instruction: An essay opening on the judgement rather than the subject.

name: el plus infinitive
instruction: A whole action, often compound, as the subject of a judgement.
examples: El haber llegado tarde le costó el puesto

name: Understatement
instruction: Praising or condemning by denying the opposite.
